title: Incident Management Process
body:
Incident Management Process
Owner: Technology (Site Reliability Engineering)
Author: Angelica Schneider, Senior Engineer
Last updated: 2026-09-29

Purpose and Scope
This procedure defines how Halcyon Ridge Capital detects, declares, manages, and reviews production incidents affecting any firm system, from MarketDataFeed and OMS through to HRIS. It applies to Technology, Trading, Wealth Management, Lending, M&A Advisory, Compliance, Risk, and Operations staff. Security incidents and suspected data exposure follow this process but are also escalated to Compliance as described below.

Severity Levels
Sev1: A critical system is down or materially degraded, or there is regulatory, financial, or market impact. Examples: OMS unavailable during market hours, PaymentsGateway failing wires, AuthSSO outage, SanctionsScreen or AMLMonitor not processing.
Sev2: A critical system is partially degraded with a workaround, or a standard system is down for a business-critical function. Examples: ReportingBI stale before a regulatory deadline, PortfolioMgr rebalancing failures.
Sev3: Limited impact on a standard or legacy system, no immediate business deadline at risk. Example: a failed ReconLegacy batch with time to rerun.
Sev4: Cosmetic or low-impact issue, handled through the normal ticket queue.
When in doubt, declare higher and downgrade later.

Roles
Incident Commander (IC): Runs the response, assigns work, and decides on severity changes. For Sev1 and Sev2 the IC is the on-call SRE (Omar Brown or Barbara Beard in the current rotation) unless the Director of Engineering, Sam Okafor, takes over.
Technical Lead: The engineer from the owning team of the affected system.
Communications Lead: Posts updates and keeps stakeholders informed. Defaults to the IC for Sev2 and below, and to a delegate named by the IC for Sev1.
Business Liaison: A representative from the impacted desk or function, such as Daniel Reyes for Trading, Ravi Patel for Operations, Grace Lin for Wealth Management, or Brian Kowalski for Lending.

Detection and Declaration
Incidents are detected by monitoring alerts, user reports, or vendor notices. Anyone can declare an incident. Post in #incidents with the affected system, observed symptoms, start time, and your best severity estimate. The on-call SRE acknowledges within 10 minutes for Sev1 and 30 minutes for Sev2, opens a ticket, and names the IC in the thread. Use #it-ops for general technology questions, and keep #incidents reserved for active incidents and status updates.

Dependency-Aware Triage
Before chasing symptoms, check upstream systems. Many incidents are downstream effects of a single root cause.
- MarketDataFeed problems surface in PricingSvc, then in RiskEngine, OMS, TradeBlotter, and PortfolioMgr.
- AuthSSO problems affect OMS, ClientHub, and DocVault, and indirectly KYCPipeline, SARFiling, and LoanOrigination.
- DataLake problems affect FraudScore, AMLMonitor, CreditScoring, and ReportingBI.
- GLCore problems affect SettlementEngine, PaymentsGateway, ReconLegacy, and ReportingBI.
The IC should open one parent incident and link downstream alerts to it rather than running parallel incidents.

Response Steps
1. Stabilize: Prefer rollback, failover, or feature flag over a forward fix during an active Sev1 or Sev2.
2. Keep a timeline in the incident thread, noting every action with a timestamp.
3. Freeze non-essential deployments to affected systems and their dependencies until the IC lifts the freeze.
4. Use the weekly-published runbook for the system if one exists. ReconLegacy runs on Perl and Oracle 11g and is best-effort only, so engage its Technology owner early and coordinate reruns with Operations in #recon.

Communication Cadence
Sev1: Update in #incidents every 30 minutes, with a note to the Executive Office (Linda Brandt as COO) at declaration and at resolution. Sev2: Update every 60 minutes. Sev3: Update at start and resolution. Updates state impact, current theory, next step, and next update time. Do not speculate on causes in broad channels.

Compliance and Risk Escalation
Notify Compliance (Marcus Bell) immediately if an incident touches SanctionsScreen, AMLMonitor, FraudScore, KYCPipeline, or SARFiling, or involves possible unauthorized access to client records in DocVault or ClientHub. Notify Risk (Owen Gallagher) if RiskEngine or market data used for exposure calculations is degraded, so that manual limit monitoring can start. Any gap in screening or monitoring must be documented so Compliance can assess regulatory reporting obligations.

Ownership Change Notice
KYCPipeline moves from Operations to Compliance ownership on 2026-10-06. Until then, KYCPipeline incidents are led by Operations. From that date, Compliance is the owning team and supplies the Technical Lead, with Technology supporting. Runbooks and the on-call escalation list will be updated on the same date.

Resolution and Post-Incident Review
The IC closes the incident once service is verified healthy by the owning team and the business liaison. A blameless post-incident review is required within five business days for Sev1 and Sev2. It covers the timeline, root cause, detection gaps, what went well, and action items with owners and due dates. Reviews are filed in the engineering wiki and summarized in #incidents. Action items are tracked as tickets and reviewed monthly by Sam Okafor and Linda Brandt.

Document Maintenance
This procedure is reviewed quarterly. Send suggested changes to Angelica Schneider or post them in #it-ops.
